failures.description: An arrow from the reference V grid straight down into the weighted-contributions grid ran through x=745, which is exactly the centre of that grid's 'flows' column header (columnLabels are drawn as a solid row spanning almost the full grid width, so a vertical entry from directly above will cross one of them almost regardless of x). Removed the arrow - V sits directly above 'weight x value' and the two labels ('value (V) - for reference', 'weight x value') already say the relationship, the same reasoning case01 used for tokens -> Q/K/V.

notesForReusableSystem: THIRD case in a row (01, 02, 04) where a straight-line arrow crossed a label and had to be manually rerouted or removed. All three were authoring fixes, not renderer bugs - arrows draw exactly where authored, and every fix was either a coordinate change or an omission-in-favour-of-alignment. This is now a clear pattern worth naming explicitly rather than re-discovering per case: there is no collision check between an authored arrow and another object's label/shape, so avoiding it costs one render-and-look cycle every time a stage sits close to a grid with column or row labels. A dev-time lint (arrow bounding line intersects another object's label rect -> warn) would remove the render-and-look cost, but this is authoring tooling, not a rendering defect - nothing is drawn incorrectly, so it does not block the run. Recording it as the interval finding rather than fixing it mid-run.
